questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify the effect of expansionary fiscal policy on aggregate demand
questions.stem: Amateur astronomer Maya logs a recessionary gap; which fiscal action raises aggregate demand?

options.text: Increase government spending and reduce taxes to lift aggregate demand
Decrease government spending and raise taxes to cool inflation
Raise reserve requirements to free bank lending capacity
options.misconception: mixes monetary tools with fiscal policy

options.text: Sell government bonds to inject liquidity into markets

questions.explanation: Expansionary fiscal policy raises aggregate demand by boosting spending or cutting taxes; contractionary tools would deepen the gap.

options.text: Cut spending and raise taxes to reduce aggregate demand
Lower reserve requirements to expand bank lending
Buy bonds to lower interest rates and boost investment
options.misconception: confuses monetary easing with fiscal tightening

questions.explanation: Contractionary fiscal policy reduces aggregate demand by cutting spending or raising taxes; monetary easing would worsen inflation.
questions.hint: Cooling means less spending or higher taxes.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Amateur astronomer Leo asks why a tax rebate shifts aggregate demand instead of causing a movement along it.

answer.exemplar: A tax rebate raises disposable income, which increases consumption at every price level, so the whole aggregate demand curve shifts right rather than moving along it.

questions.explanation: A tax rebate changes spending at all price levels, shifting aggregate demand; a price change alone would cause movement along the curve.
questions.hint: Shifters change spending at every price level.
